idea: A website where my gym friends log workouts and see a weekly leaderboard

result.restatement: A website where gym friends log workouts and view a weekly leaderboard.

decisions.question: How should the website be built and shown to users?
decisions.choice: A React framework that renders pages on the server and in the browser.
decisions.why: It handles pages, API routes, and deployment in one tool, which keeps a beginner project simple.
decisions.tradeoffs: More to learn than a plain HTML file, but less setup than separate frontend and backend projects.

alternatives.name: Vite + React
alternatives.betterWhen: You want a lightweight frontend only and will host a separate backend.

alternatives.name: Plain HTML and JavaScript
alternatives.betterWhen: You want zero build tools and only need a single static page.

decisions.question: Where will the server code and API live?
decisions.choice: Server-side functions inside the same Next.js project that answer browser requests.
decisions.why: No separate server project is needed, so the workout log and leaderboard can share one codebase.
decisions.tradeoffs: Less flexible than a standalone backend if the app grows very large.

alternatives.name: Express
alternatives.betterWhen: You want a dedicated Node.js server separate from the frontend.

alternatives.name: Supabase Edge Functions
alternatives.betterWhen: You prefer serverless functions hosted with your database.

decisions.question: Where should workout data live?
decisions.choice: A relational database that stores users, workouts, and leaderboard rows in tables.
decisions.why: It fits structured workout records and is widely supported by low-cost hosts.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires defining a schema upfront, unlike a document database.

alternatives.name: SQLite
alternatives.betterWhen: You want a single-file database with no separate server for local development.

alternatives.name: MongoDB
alternatives.betterWhen: Your workout records have very different shapes and you want flexible documents.

decisions.question: How will users sign in and stay signed in?
decisions.choice: Users register with an email and password, which is verified on sign-in.
decisions.why: Simple to understand and does not require setting up external providers.
decisions.tradeoffs: You must securely hash passwords and manage sessions yourself.

alternatives.name: OAuth
alternatives.betterWhen: You want users to sign in with Google or Apple instead of creating a new password.

alternatives.name: Supabase Auth
alternatives.betterWhen: You want ready-made sign-in pages and session handling without building them.

decisions.question: Where will the website be published?
decisions.choice: A platform that deploys Next.js projects with a git push and provides a free tier.
decisions.why: It works well with Next.js and requires little configuration for a beginner.
decisions.tradeoffs: Serverless functions have limits, which is fine for a small gym group.

alternatives.name: Railway
alternatives.betterWhen: You need a separate backend server or database in the same deploy.

alternatives.name: Netlify
alternatives.betterWhen: You prefer a similar git-based deploy platform with form handling.

firstSteps: Create a GitHub repository for the project.
Run `npx create-next-app@latest` in an empty folder.
Add a PostgreSQL database on a free host and save its connection string in `.env.local`.
Create a `workouts` table with columns for user, exercise, sets, reps, weight, and date.
Build a page with a form to submit a workout and a page to show the weekly leaderboard.
Deploy to Vercel by connecting the GitHub repository.

# AGENTS.md

## What this is
A website where gym friends log workouts and view a weekly leaderboard.

## Stack
- Next.js
- React
- PostgreSQL
- Prisma
- Vercel

## Structure
- /app - pages and API routes
- /src/lib - database client and helpers
- /src/components - reusable UI pieces
- /prisma - database schema and migrations

## How to work
- Build one small step at a time. Explain the plan before changing many files.
- Commit after every working change with a clear message.
- Ask before adding a dependency. Prefer none.
- If something fails, say so plainly. Do not hide it.

## Rules
- Never log passwords or connection strings to the console.
- Validate workout inputs before saving to the database.
- Use environment variables for database URLs and secrets.
- Keep API routes in `/app/api` and UI components in `/src/components`.
- Return clear error messages when a workout fails to save.

## Security
- Never commit secrets. Keep them in a gitignored env file and in the host's secret store.
- Validate all input. Never put user text into the page with innerHTML.
